kept.title: Incorrect filtering of 'this$' properties removed in v1 decoder readObject
kept.explanation: The change removed the check that omitted properties with keys matching /^this\$\d+$/ in the readObject method of the v1 decoder. This causes properties like 'this$0' to be included in the decoded object, changing semantics and breaking compatibility with prior expectations and test cases.
kept.suggestion: Restore the filtering to exclude keys matching /^this\$\d+$/ when reading object properties in v1 decoder readObject.
kept.failureAfterChange: Decoding an object with a property named 'this$0' now includes it in the output object, whereas before it was excluded. This breaks backward compatibility and test expectations.

kept.title: Incorrect filtering of 'this$' properties removed in v2 decoder readObject
kept.explanation: Similar to v1, the filter that omitted properties with keys matching /^this\$\d+$/ was removed in the v2 decoder's readObject method. This causes properties like 'this$0' to be included in the decoded object, which may break expectations and compatibility.
kept.suggestion: Restore the filtering to exclude keys matching /^this\$\d+$/ when reading object properties in v2 decoder readObject.
kept.failureAfterChange: Decoding an object with a property named 'this$0' in v2 now includes it in the output, potentially breaking compatibility with previous behavior and tests.

verdicts.reason: The finding identifies a concrete defect introduced by the change in lib/v1/decoder.js. The removed filtering for keys matching /^this\$\d+$/ leads to inclusion of properties like 'this$0' which previously were excluded. This breaks backward compatibility and test expectations, so the finding should be kept.

Similarly, in lib/v2/decoder.js the removal of filtering for keys matching /^this\$\d+$/ causes inclusion of these properties in the decoded object, changing the output and breaking compatibility. This is a concrete defect introduced by the change and thus the finding should be kept.
